q-51229.name: Question 1
q-51229.worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u={x}^{3}+x$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}^{3}+x$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ |  |  |
| $3{x}^{2}+1$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ | $+$ | $({x}^{3}+x)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $6x$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}$ | $-$ | $(3{x}^{2}+1)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |
| $6$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{8}$ | $+$ | $-\frac{3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{16}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{3}+x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =({x}^{3}+x)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+(3{x}^{2}+1)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}-\frac{3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}-\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}+C \\  & =(2{x}^{3}-x)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+(6{x}^{2}-1)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-14779.worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u=2{x}^{4}+4$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2{x}^{4}+4$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ |  |  |
| $8{x}^{3}$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}$ | $+$ | $\frac{(2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}$ |
| $24{x}^{2}$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}$ | $-$ | $\frac{8{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}$ |
| $48x$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{27}$ | $+$ | $-\frac{8{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}$ |
| $48$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{81}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{16x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{243}$ | $+$ | $\frac{16\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{8{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}-\frac{8{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}-\frac{16x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}+\frac{16\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}+C \\  & =(54{x}^{4}-72{x}^{2}+124)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}+(24{x}^{3}-16x)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}+C\end{aligned}
$$

| $12x+6$ | $-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ | $-$ | $(6{x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ |
| $12$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ | $+$ | $(12x+6)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ |

$$

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same Color Products
2x3+3x2+5 sin⁡(x)

12x+6 −sin⁡(x) − (6x2+6x)sin⁡(x)

q-13148.name: Question 4
q-13148.worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ |  |  |
| $3{x}^{2}+6x$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ | $+$ | $\frac{({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $6x+6$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}$ | $-$ | $\frac{(3{x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |
| $6$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{8}$ | $+$ | $-\frac{(3x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{16}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{(3{x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}-\frac{(3x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}-\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}+C \\  & =(2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-3x-3)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+(6{x}^{2}+12x-3)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-104069.worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u=2{x}^{3}$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2{x}^{3}$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ |  |  |
| $6{x}^{2}$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}$ | $+$ | $-{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ |
| $12x$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ | $-$ | $\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $12$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}$ | $+$ | $\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{16}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C \\  & =(3x-2{x}^{3})\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+(6{x}^{2}-3)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Evaluate ∫(2x3+3x2+5)e2xdx.

a
e2x4(x3+2x+5)+C
b
e2x2(2x3+6x+5)+C
c
e2x2(5x3+2)+C
d
e2x2(2x3+5)+C
e
e2x4(3x3+5x+6)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For this integral, we choose u=2x3+3x2+5 and dvdx=e2x. Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
2x3+3x2+5 e2x
6x2+6x e2x2 + (2x3+3x2+5)e2x2
12x+6 e2x4 − −(3x2+3x)e2x2
12 e2x8 + (6x+3)e2x4
0 e2x16 − −3e2x4

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

∫(2x3+3x2+5)e2xdx=e2x4[2(2x3+3x2+5)−2(3x2+3x)+(6x+3)−3]+C=e2x4(4x3+10)+C=e2x2(2x3+5)+C

| $24{x}^{2}$ | $\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{{x}^{3}{e}^{4x}}{2}$ |
| $48x$ | $\frac{{e}^{4x}}{64}$ | $+$ | $\frac{3{x}^{2}{e}^{4x}}{8}$ |
| $48$ | $\frac{{e}^{4x}}{256}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{16}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\int 2{x}^{4}{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{64}(32{x}^{4}-32{x}^{3}+24{x}^{2}-12x+3)+C
$$

q-14780.worked_solution:
For this integral, we choose $u=4{x}^{4}+2$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4{x}^{4}+2$ | ${e}^{x}$ |  |  |
| $16{x}^{3}$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $(4{x}^{4}+2){e}^{x}$ |
| $48{x}^{2}$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $-$ | $-16{x}^{3}{e}^{x}$ |
| $96x$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $48{x}^{2}{e}^{x}$ |
| $96$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $-$ | $-96x{e}^{x}$ |
| $0$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $96{e}^{x}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{4}+2){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}(4{x}^{4}-16{x}^{3}+48{x}^{2}-96x+98)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ∫(4x4+2)exdx.

a
ex(3x4−12x3+48x2−96x−98)+C
b
e2x(3x4−12x3+48x2−96x+98)+C
c
ex(4x4+16x3+48x2−96x+98)+C

ex(4x4−16x3+48x2−96x+98)+C
e
ex(3x4−12x3−48x2−96x+98)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For this integral, we choose u=4x4+2 and dvdx=ex. Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
4x4+2 ex
16x3 ex + (4x4+2)ex
48x2 ex − −16x3ex
96x ex + 48x2ex
96 ex − −96xex
0 ex + 96ex

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. ∫(4x4+2)exdx=ex(4x4−16x3+48x2−96x+98)+C

q-14778.worked_solution:
For this integral, we choose $u=4{x}^{4}+4$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4{x}^{4}+4$ | ${e}^{2x}$ |  |  |
| $16{x}^{3}$ | $\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}$ | $+$ | $(2{x}^{4}+2){e}^{2x}$ |
| $48{x}^{2}$ | $\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}$ | $-$ | $-4{x}^{3}{e}^{2x}$ |
| $96x$ | $\frac{{e}^{2x}}{8}$ | $+$ | $6{x}^{2}{e}^{2x}$ |
| $96$ | $\frac{{e}^{2x}}{16}$ | $-$ | $-6x{e}^{2x}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{{e}^{2x}}{32}$ | $+$ | $3{e}^{2x}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{4}+4){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{2x}(2{x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-6x+5)+C\end{aligned}
$$

?

∫(4x4+4)e2xdx=

a
e2x(2x4−4x3+6x2−6x+5)+C
b
e2x2(4x4−6x3+6x2−6x+5)+C
c
e2x4(x4+2x3+6x2−6x−5)+C
d
e2x(4x4+2x3−6x2−6x−5)+C
e
e2x4(2x4−4x3−3x2+6x+5)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For this integral, we choose u=4x4+4 and dvdx=e2x. Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
4x4+4 e2x
16x3 e2x2 + (2x4+2)e2x
48x2 e2x4 − −4x3e2x
96x e2x8 + 6x2e2x
96 e2x16 − −6xe2x
0 e2x32 + 3e2x

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. ∫(4x4+4)e2xdx=e2x(2x4−4x3+6x2−6x+5)+C

Evaluate ∫(2x4+4x)e3xdx.

a
2e3x27(27x4+36x3−36x2+10x−20)+C
b
e3x81(20x4+36x3+36x2+10x−27)+C
c
e3x81(27x4−27x3+36x2+20x−20)+C
d
2e3x81(27x4−36x3+36x2+30x−10)+C
e
e3x27(27x4+36x3−36x2+30x−10)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For this integral, we choose u=2x4+4x and dvdx=e3x. Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
2x4+4x e3x
8x3+4 e3x3 + (2x4+4x)e3x3
24x2 e3x9 − −(8x3+4)e3x9
48x e3x27 + 8x2e3x9
48 e3x81 − −16xe3x27
0 e3x243 + 16e3x81

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

∫(2x4+4x)e3xdx=e3x81(27(2x4+4x)−9(8x3+4)+9(8x2)−3(16x)+16)+C=e3x81(54x4−72x3+72x2+60x−20)+C=2e3x81(27x4−36x3+36x2+30x−10)+C
